title: Bound the status call in the predates-stop hint with a timeout
lead: S56 added a status call to the hint that `ork daemon stop` and `ork daemon restart` print for a daemon that predates daemon.stop (roleMayRun, internal/cli/lifecycle.go:164-190, called from predatesStop at :146-163). The call passes the command's context and sets no timeout. A daemon that accepts the connection but never answers status would stall the command. Noted in the S56 run report.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: The command exists to deal with a daemon that cannot be told to stop. A hung status call turns the hint into a hang on exactly that daemon.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- internal/cli/lifecycle.go: roleMayRun (:164-190) and its caller predatesStop (:146-163).
- internal/cli/lifecycle_test.go: a test beside TestDaemonStopPredatingDaemon, using a fake daemon that answers daemon.stop with unknown_method and never answers status.
- docs/design.md: the stop and restart paragraph that describes the hint (find it with rg -n "predates" docs/design.md).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- Against a fake daemon that answers daemon.stop with unknown_method and never answers status, `ork daemon stop` and `ork daemon restart` still print the guidance within the timeout, with the warning that a role may be running, and exit 1.
- The existing TestDaemonStopPredatingDaemon cases still pass.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Wrap the context passed to roleMayRun in context.WithTimeout. Open: the timeout value. Candidates are the existing defaultStartWait (5s, internal/cli/cli.go:29) or a new constant; the owner has not decided. Settle it with `adj ask` before this slice runs. On expiry the status call fails and the existing "a role may be running" warning prints.
